title: Dhurandhar Sweeps DPIFF Awards 2026 as Taylor Swift, James Cameron Take Global Honours
excerpt: The privately organised Dadasaheb Phalke International Film Festival named 41 winners in Mumbai on November 20 — Best Film and Best Actor for Dhurandhar, Best Actress for Aneet Padda, and an International Artist of the Year title for Taylor Swift.
body:
• The Dadasaheb Phalke International Film Festival (DPIFF) announced its 2026 winners on November 20, 2026, in Mumbai — 41 categories across film, web series, television, music, short films and international cinema.
  • Dhurandhar led the Indian film honours: Best Film, Best Actor for Ranveer Singh, Best Director for Aditya Dhar, Best Actor in a Negative Role for Akshaye Khanna and Best Music Director for Shashwat Sachdev.
  • One distinction matters: DPIFF is a privately organised festival, not the Government of India's Dadasaheb Phalke Award, the national film honour named for the same pioneer.
  • The international list named Taylor Swift International Artist of the Year and honoured James Cameron for Outstanding Contribution in Global Cinema; Avatar: Fire and Ash was named Best International Feature Film.

The Dadasaheb Phalke International Film Festival Awards 2026 were announced on November 20, 2026, in Mumbai, with winners across 41 categories published by the festival on its official accounts. The night belonged, in the Indian film categories, to Dhurandhar: the espionage thriller took Best Film, Best Actor for Ranveer Singh and Best Director for Aditya Dhar, while Aditya Dhar, Jyoti Deshpande and Lokesh Dhar were jointly named Producer of the Year.

First, which award is this?

The name causes confusion every year, so it is worth stating plainly. DPIFF is a privately organised awards platform — an independent festival founded in 2012, per The Times of Bengal's winners report — that takes its name from Dadasaheb Phalke, the father of Indian cinema. It is not the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, the lifetime honour presented by the Government of India with the National Film Awards. The winners below are DPIFF's, announced by the festival itself.

The Indian film honours

Beyond the top prizes, Dhurandhar also won Best Actor in a Negative Role for Akshaye Khanna and Best Music Director for Shashwat Sachdev. Aneet Padda was named Best Actress for Saiyaara, which carried the music categories: Song of the Year for its title track, Best Lyricist for Irshad Kamil and Best Playback Singer for Faheem Abdullah. Vineet Kumar Singh won Best Actor in a Supporting Role for Chhaava, and Riteish Deshmukh Best Actor in a Comic Role for Housefull 5.

The critics' prizes went south and to a courtroom drama: Kantara: Chapter 1 was Critics Best Film, Rishab Shetty Critics Best Actor, and its cinematographer Arvind S. Kashyap won Best Cinematographer; Yami Gautam Dhar was Critics Best Actress for Haq, which also won Best Screenplay and Dialogue for Reshu Nath. Kamal Haasan received Outstanding Contribution in Film Industry, and Ilaiyaraaja Outstanding Contribution in Music Industry. Karan Aujla was named Artist of the Year.

Streaming and television

The Ba**ds of Bollywood was named Best Web Series, and Aryan Khan Best Director in a Web Series for it. Jaideep Ahlawat won Best Actor in a Web Series for Paatal Lok Season 2, and Shefali Shah Best Actress in a Web Series for Delhi Crime Season 3, with Huma Qureshi winning Best Actress in a Negative Role for the same series. On television, Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah was named Television Series of the Year, and Smriti Irani and Amar Upadhyay took the top TV acting honours for Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi 2. Comedian Samay Raina was named Comedian of the Year.

The international list

DPIFF's international categories explain the names that raised eyebrows on social media. Taylor Swift was named International Artist of the Year — a festival honour announced online, which is why fans asked whether she knew. James Cameron received Outstanding Contribution in Global Cinema, and his Avatar: Fire and Ash was named Best International Feature Film. Michael B. Jordan won Best Actor in an International Feature Film for Sinners, Jessie Buckley Best Actress for Hamnet, and Paul Thomas Anderson Best Director in an International Feature Film for One Battle After Another.

The complete 41-category list, including the short-film winners, is published in Jagran Josh's category-wise compilation and in Filmibeat's report. Read the list for what it is — one private festival's picks, with a genuinely strong year for Dhurandhar, Saiyaara and Kantara: Chapter 1 — rather than as a national honour.
